question: Should OpenClaw permit a native compaction result produced after the safety-timeout abort to commit session state during a bounded acceptance window?
rationale: This changes the semantic boundary between terminal cancellation and authoritative session-state commitment; tests can validate an implementation, but they cannot choose that product and ownership policy.

options.title: Adopt typed partial outcome
options.body: Approve bounded partial-progress commitment, but require an explicit typed outcome owned by compaction/session code plus native end-to-end timeout proof before merge.

options.title: Keep timeout terminal
options.body: Retain terminal safety-timeout cancellation and narrow this PR to provider-side timeout partial summaries and user guidance.

options.title: Accept current timing bridge
options.body: Approve the `WeakSet` and microtask acceptance window as the intended session-state contract after the central path and conflicts are repaired.

recommendation.title: Adopt typed partial outcome
recommendation.body: Approve bounded partial-progress commitment, but require an explicit typed outcome owned by compaction/session code plus native end-to-end timeout proof before merge.
